Round 3, re-read. The whole bullet: 'Separately, pro-Russian groups NoName057(16) and Z-Pentest have claimed the November wave of supermarket attacks. Investigators have not confirmed those claims, and one research firm doubts the groups did more than claim credit. No source reports that they claimed the October attack.' The 'competing account' problem is fixed and the first two statements hold. Scope is now stated and matches the sources: TechTimes: the groups 'claimed joint responsibility' for the November wave; Anadolu, Nov. 4: claim concerns Monday's incidents; Nordisk Post, Nov. 5: attacks 'across Europe this week', discovered Monday 2 November; Cybernews: 'claimed shared responsibility for the recent attacks'. Help Net Security: 'investigators haven't confirmed the claim'. Two things are still off. (1) Who doubts: not a research firm. Cybernews: 'a threat intelligence researcher going under the name CyberKnow on X' who 'expressed doubts about whether the hacktivists had actually breached the systems'; TechTimes: 'A threat-intelligence researcher known as CyberKnow'. A pseudonymous individual on X has been given a firm's weight. SentinelOne, the firm on the source list, says only that the claims 'have not been independently verified'. (2) 'No source reports' is a universal the page cannot know; it can only say what it found. I read seven accounts (Help Net Security, Cybernews, Anadolu, TechTimes, SentinelOne, Nordisk Post, Liga) and none reports a claim on October; Nordisk Post adds investigators 'have not established whether the October and November incidents had the same perpetrators'. That supports 'we found no report', not 'no source reports'. The universal was in my round 2 suggested wording; that was my error. Neither Cybernews nor TechTimes, where the doubt comes from, is linked in the source list.
verdicts.fix: Separately, pro-Russian groups NoName057(16) and Z-Pentest have claimed the November wave of supermarket attacks. Investigators have not confirmed those claims, and one threat researcher doubts the groups did more than claim credit. We found no report that they claimed the October attack.

flags: Round 3. 82 ledger claims plus 22 extras (x001-x013 timeline events in var E; x014 the id='update' paragraph; x015-x022 device cards in var D). Changed since round 2 and re-read: c003, c050, c070, c073, c075 (whole checkpoint), x013, x014, x015, plus the untagged timeline note. c051 and c052 changed in the ledger only because the extractor pulls the neighbouring Apple sentence into their text. Everything else carried by text match.

How the text match was done: the ledger on disk had again been regenerated before my run, so I rebuilt the round 2 page in memory by reverting the five revised passages to their round 2 wording, ran the extractor's own function on it, got the round 2 sha (8ac55f04709bb4b4) exactly, and diffed that against the new ledger.
